issues.body: `npm_test_targets()` scans all of `rest` for `--workspaces`, `-ws`, and workspace selectors without stopping at npm's `--` delimiter. Thus `npm test -- --workspaces` returns `ALL_WORKSPACES`, even though `--workspaces` is passed to the test script and npm runs only the test selected by the effective working directory. Likewise, `npm run test -- --workspace packages/x` falsely credits `packages/x`. This is fail-open: a workflow can appear to execute every package test while executing only one.
issues.fix_hint: When parsing npm options, stop recognizing npm flags at the first standalone `--`; tokens after it are script arguments. Add negative tests showing `npm test -- --workspaces` targets only the current working directory and `npm run test -- --workspace packages/x` does not credit `packages/x`, while retaining positive tests for selectors before the delimiter.
issues.title: Script arguments after `--` are misread as npm workspace selectors

verdict.summary: The prior allowlist bypass is fixed with fail-closed validation and meaningful negative tests. However, the npm command parser now has a separate fail-open case: it continues interpreting tokens after npm's `--` argument delimiter as npm workspace flags. A workflow command that runs only its current package's test can therefore be credited as testing an arbitrary package or every workspace. Because this can silently satisfy the repo-wide invariant without executing those packages' tests, the change is not yet safe to approve. This is a new major finding, so progress is regressing under the required comparison scale.
